beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A garden. Two trees. And the whole plan balanced between them. Eden was not a paradise for lounging. It was the first classroom — and the lesson was choice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: God planted the garden eastward in Eden, and put the man and the woman in it. Innocent. Deathless. Safe. And — read it carefully — not yet able to grow.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And they would have had no children; wherefore they would have remained in a state of innocence, having no joy, for they knew no misery; doing no good, for they knew no sin.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No joy — because no misery. No good — because no sin. Frozen. Eden was beautiful the way a photograph is beautiful. Perfect, and going nowhere.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So God did something the critics never notice. He put two trees in the middle — the tree of life, and the tree of knowledge — and gave the one commandment that made choosing real. Listen to how He actually said it:

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat, but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it. Nevertheless, thou mayest choose for thyself, for it is given unto thee; but, remember that I forbid it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Thou mayest choose for thyself. Did you catch that? The forbidden tree came with a permission slip. God fenced it with a warning — and left the gate unlocked on purpose. Because a choice with only one option is not a choice.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Wherefore, the Lord God gave unto man that he should act for himself. Wherefore, man could not act for himself save it should be that he was enticed by the one or the other.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Enticed by the one or the other. Opposition is not sabotage of the plan — it is equipment. And right on schedule, the other enticement slid into the garden.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The serpent came carrying the first lie ever told on this earth. Listen closely. You have heard this voice before.

beats.speaker: devil
beats.text: Ye shall not surely die; for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Half-truths stitched with poison — his signature ever since. Their eyes would open; that part was true. But underneath it was the council pitch all over again: trust me instead of Him. He wanted the fall to happen his way. Under his flag.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And here is what he has never once understood. He thought he was wrecking God's plan. He was springing it. The fall was always the doorway — the only question was whose hand would open the door.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Eve weighed it. Scripture says she saw the tree was to be desired to make one wise. This was not a fooled woman blundering. It was the bravest decision ever made in innocence. She chose growth. Adam chose to stay with her. And the door opened.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So the next time someone tells you Eden was the day everything went wrong, remember the two trees. God planted both. He named the price, honored the choice, and had the rescue already signed. That is not a God who lost control. That is a Father who refused to keep His children in a photograph.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: Eden was not the day it all went wrong. It was the day it all began.
